title: Canonical condensed realizations of the base p-adic coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and the normed algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with its norm extending the $\ell$-adic norm. Let $E_0\subset\Omega$ be the image of the structural embedding $\iota:\mathbf Q_\ell\hookrightarrow\Omega$, regarded as the bottom finite intermediate field. Give $E_0$ its subspace norm and set $\mathcal O_{E_0}=\{x\in E_0:\lVert x\rVert\le1\}$; similarly $\mathbf Z_\ell=\{x\in\mathbf Q_\ell:\lVert x\rVert\le1\}$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Write $\underline R$ for the commutative condensed ring whose sections on a profinite set $S$ are continuous functions $S\to R$, with pointwise operations [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring].

The maps $q\mapsto\iota(q)$ and its restriction to the unit balls are isometric ring isomorphisms
$$e:\mathbf Q_\ell\xrightarrow{\sim}E_0,\qquad e^\circ:\mathbf Z_\ell\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{E_0}.$$
They induce ring-object isomorphisms
$$\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{E_0},\qquad \underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{\mathcal O}_{E_0},$$
whose components on every profinite $S$ are postcomposition by $e$ and $e^\circ$, respectively. These components and their inverses commute with restriction along continuous maps of profinite sets, and the integral isomorphism followed by $\underline{\mathcal O}_{E_0}\to\underline{E_0}$ equals the rational isomorphism preceded by $\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell\to\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.

source.place: Introductory coefficient specializations: 'it suffices to treat A, O_E, E and Qlb'; det-existence-localizing.proof.md introductory sentence identifying Z_l and Q_l with O_E and E for E=Q_l.

proof.text: Define $e(q)=\iota(q)$, with codomain restricted to $E_0=\operatorname{im}(\iota)$. It preserves $0,1,+,\cdot$ because $\iota$ is a ring embedding. For $x\in E_0$, membership in this image gives a $q\in\mathbf Q_\ell$ with $\iota(q)=x$, and injectivity of $\iota$ makes $q$ unique. Define $r(x)=q$. Then $r(e(q))=q$ and $e(r(x))=x$. Applying $e$ to $r(x+y)$ and $r(x)+r(y)$ gives $x+y$ in both cases, so injectivity gives equality; the same calculation proves preservation of multiplication, zero and one. Thus $e$ and $r$ are inverse ring homomorphisms.

source.place: Opening paragraph: the Z_l and Q_l cases are O_E and E with E=Q_l; explicit elementary verification of the structural-image identifications.

proof.text: The subspace norm and the hypothesis that the norm of $\Omega$ extends the base norm give $\lVert e(q)\rVert=\lVert\iota(q)\rVert=\lVert q\rVert$. Consequently $d(e(q),e(q'))=\lVert\iota(q-q')\rVert=\lVert q-q'\rVert=d(q,q')$. Substituting $q=r(x)$ and $q'=r(x')$ gives $d(r(x),r(x'))=d(x,x')$. Thus $e$ and $r$ are isometries. They are continuous: for every $\epsilon>0$, choose $\delta=\epsilon$ in the definition of continuity, and use these distance equalities.

source.place: Opening paragraph: the Z_l and Q_l cases are O_E and E with E=Q_l; explicit elementary verification of the structural-image identifications.

proof.text: The ring of integers in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] is the unit ball; here the item specifies its norm to be the restricted norm. Norm preservation gives $\lVert q\rVert\le1$ if and only if $\lVert e(q)\rVert\le1$. Hence restrict $e$ to $e^\circ:\mathbf Z_\ell\to\mathcal O_{E_0}$ and $r$ to $r^\circ:\mathcal O_{E_0}\to\mathbf Z_\ell$. Their inverse identities and ring identities are the identities of step 1 restricted to the subrings. Their distances are unchanged by passing to the subspace metrics, so the equalities of step 2 show that both restrictions are isometries and continuous. This proves the asserted integral isometric ring isomorphism.

source.place: Opening paragraph: the Z_l and Q_l cases are O_E and E with E=Q_l; explicit elementary verification of the structural-image identifications.

proof.text: Use the continuous-ring-map construction of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] on each of $e,r,e^\circ,r^\circ$. For a profinite set $S$, the resulting maps are $a\mapsto e\circ a$, $b\mapsto r\circ b$ and their integral versions. These are continuous functions because the scalar maps are continuous. Pointwise, $e(a+a')=e(a)+e(a')$, $e(aa')=e(a)e(a')$, $e(1)=1$, and the analogous identities hold for the other three scalar maps; hence the section maps preserve the ring operations. Moreover $r\circ(e\circ a)=a$ and $e\circ(r\circ b)=b$, with the identical formulas for $r^\circ,e^\circ$. Thus the two pairs of condensed ring morphisms are inverse. Their underlying abelian-sheaf morphisms preserve multiplication and unit by these same pointwise identities, so they are the asserted isomorphisms of commutative ring objects.

source.place: Opening paragraph: the Z_l and Q_l cases are O_E and E with E=Q_l; explicit elementary verification of the structural-image identifications.

proof.text: Restriction in [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] is precomposition. For a continuous $u:T\to S$ and $a:S\to\mathbf Q_\ell$, both $(e\circ a)\circ u$ and $e\circ(a\circ u)$ send $t$ to $e(a(u(t)))$. Replacing $e$ by $r,e^\circ,r^\circ$ proves the required naturality also for both inverses. Finally let $j:\mathbf Z_\ell\to\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $j_0:\mathcal O_{E_0}\to E_0$ be the inclusions. For $z\in\mathbf Z_\ell$, $j_0(e^\circ(z))=\iota(z)=e(j(z))$, by the definition as a restriction. Postcomposing a section $a:S\to\mathbf Z_\ell$ gives $j_0\circ e^\circ\circ a=e\circ j\circ a$, proving the stated compatibility of the integral and rational condensed isomorphisms.
